title: GPU fleet sprint tactical logbook - 2026-06-21
content:
Sprint logbook: operational standup + tactical notes (week of 2026-06-21)

Summary:
- Short: Smooth week overall; regional tail-latency noise in eu-west persisted after the kernel patch but traffic shaping and temporary placement rules reduced customer impact to <0.4% error budget.
- Focus areas for next sprint: (1) firming up pre-warm schedule for new A100 batch, (2) finalize regional tagging schema for burst budgets, (3) automated reclaim play for idle burst capacity.

Attendees (quick): Aisha, Ethan, Mariana, Jacob, Priya, on-call engineer (shift B).

Highlights / Decisions:
- Decided to keep the eu-west emergency placement rule active 48 more hours while we validate a second kernel revision (INFRA-2398).
- Agreed to prototype "burst-ledger" labels on nodes to allow billing/priority decoupling for Dedicated tenants — MVP design sketched in meeting, owner: Priya.
- Approved a 3-day burn-in for the 16 A100 nodes arriving next month; infra will schedule low-priority synthetic traffic during nights to exercise PCIe and NVLink topology.

Regional status (short sweeps):
- us-west: Stable. Warm pool occupancy 78%. No preemption spikes. Observed slightly higher short-sequence throughput (10% increase) after the batching heuristic tweak (gh PR linked).
- eu-west: Persistent 95th/99th token tail spikes in the 2-6s region for customers with long context workloads. Kernel patch rolled (PR 482) reduced difference but not fully resolved. Working hypothesis: memory allocator bug interacting with fragmented cache lanes.
- apac-east: Capacity margin tight (weekend load + partner trials). We established night-time rotational backfill from dedicated buffer nodes; action to request one extra node group from capacity procurement (JIRA INFRA-2345).
- edge regions: Two small edge sites (sea-1) showing packet loss during hi-load tests; networking debug in progress with infra-net team.

Incidents & quick postmortem notes:
- Incident: eu-west tail-latency spike (2026-06-19 03:14 UTC) — root cause: allocator fragmentation after a series of heterogeneous-model rollouts. Impact: 6 customers saw degraded p99s; errors within SLA but noticeable.
  - Mitigations applied: placement rule change to isolate noisy model families; temporary conservative batch size; increased sampling for tracer.
  - Follow-ups: instrument allocator fragmentation metrics (Jacob), create crashharness cases that reproduce fragmentation pattern (Mariana).

Capacity planning snapshot:
- Current committed pool vs rolling forecast: committed 820 GPUs; effective available (after reserved/dedicated commits) 610 GPUs. Forecast for next 4 weeks shows potential ~12% demand growth due to a marketing trial + partner onboarding.
- Recommended buffer: hold 5% additional nodes in us-west and apac-east for two weeks while partner trials ramp. Approved pending procurement confirmation.
- Action: update capacity ramp spreadsheet with daily burn rates and map to business commitments (owner: Ethan).

Runbook / automation notes:
- Prewarming: New prewarm job iteration launched (v2) that warms KV caches for top-20 long-context prompts per tenant. Early results: median priming latency improved ~18% on test harness. Need to validate real traffic impact before broad rollout.
- Eviction/reclaim probe: test harness for opportunistic reclaim (idle > 4h) passed load baseline but exposed a scheduling race when two reclaimers target same node. Patch queued (INFRA-2398).
- Cost smoothing: prototype script that re-routes low-priority batch jobs into Dedicated burst slots during underutil windows; initial backtest shows ~7% unit-cost reduction for mixed workloads.

Experiments in flight:
- KV cache warmers (A/B): running with 8 tenants; metrics: token-per-cost delta, p95 latency, cache hit rate. Initial: hit rate +12%, overall token cost +1% (acceptable trade).
- Preemptible fill (spot) trials: running 48h window to measure preemption churn and warm-up cost; early note: average churn 2.8/hr for the cheap cohort, adjust checkpoint cadence.
- Scheduling RNG: randomized placement vs affinity placement test to observe fragmentation; affinity reduces fragmentation at cost of slightly higher p50.

Open blockers:
- Procurement confirmation for extra apac-east node group (blocking buffer increase). Owner: Ethan, due 2026-06-24.
- Kernel revision validation for eu-west (security/perf review needed). Owner: Jacob, due 2026-06-23.
- Finalize node-label schema for burst-ledger (needs input from billing team). Owner: Priya, due 2026-06-25.

Action items (explicit):
- Priya: Draft the burst-ledger label schema + sample billing mapping and post to #billing-infra by EOD 2026-06-23.
- Jacob: Add allocator fragmentation counters to node telemetry and land the small tracing patch (INFRA-2398) by 2026-06-23.
- Mariana: Build 3 deterministic repro cases for the eu-west fragmentation pattern, attach to INFRA-2398, due 2026-06-24.
- Ethan: Update capacity ramp workbook (sheet link in Confluence) with daily burn-rate and notify procurement, due 2026-06-24.
- On-call (shift B): Keep placement rule active for eu-west until kernel validation completes; escalate immediately if customer p99s exceed 8s.

Meeting notes (weekly sync 2026-06-21):
- Quick round: each region reported.
- Terraform drift: small drift in us-west DB subnet that caused a delayed attach; PR submitted to infra-terraform (review requested).
- Observability: request to SRE to add a small dashboard widget that correlates p99 token latency with allocator-fragmentation metric. Jacob to pair with SRE.

Notes to self / working ideas (sketches):
- Consider "soft-reservation" objects for Dedicated customers so we can reclaim transiently with a TTL and payback window — might reduce idle waste.
- Explore small controlled quantization profiles for very stable families to save unit cost in Dedicated pools; needs eval harness.

References & links mentioned:
- INFRA-2345 (apac-east capacity request), INFRA-2398 (allocator tracing and reclaim race).
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet/pull/482 (batching heuristic tweak).
- Confluence: capacity-horizon-2026-06 (linked workbook).

End of logbook. Next sync: 2026-06-28 (same time).
